# Review

§7's review: three rounds at most, each finding with an id, a file and line, a severity, evidence, a fix, the commit that fixes it and the regression test that fails when the fix is reverted. Round 1 ran five fresh reviewers from briefs in `docs/build/briefs/review1_*.md`, launched together.

## Round 1

### Fact-checker (`docs/build/FACT_CHECK.md`)

All 32 claims resolve to a cached source by sha256, every quote is verbatim and at most 40 words, and 30 of 32 texts are supported as written.

| Id | File and line | Severity | Evidence | Fix | Commit | Regression test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FC-F1 | `docs/build/claims_product.json` (pc-g300-entry-timing) | minor | Text "the G300 should start in late '27 or early '28"; source "the onset of the 300, which late '27, early '28, somewhere in that", after the CEO says she no longer estimates entry into service | Deleted the claim and its sentence in the note, as §7 says; not softened | bdcd3ec | `tests/test_claims.py::test_claims_the_fact_check_removed_stay_out` |
| FC-F2 | `docs/build/claims_product.json` (pc-g300-announced) | minor | Text "Gulfstream announced"; GD's 10-Q says "we announced", the filer being General Dynamics | Deleted the claim and its sentence | bdcd3ec | same test |
| FC-F3 | `docs/build/claims_risks.json` (risk-tariffs) | minor | Supported by the FY2025 10-K, but the 2026Q2 10-Q reports tariff refunds after a February 2026 court ruling, so the present tense "continue to evolve" is stale | Dated the text to its filing: "In its 2025 annual report, GD said tariffs had not had a material impact on its results but reduced Aerospace operating margins by 30 basis points in 2025." Still supported by the same quote | bdcd3ec | `tests/test_claims.py::test_claims_quotes_are_in_their_sources` keeps the quote tied to the cited filing |

### Lock-path operator (`docs/build/review1_ops.md`)

Eleven live runs on throwaway clones (runner eve, runner release day, a conflict during a lock, two Mac runs at once, and others). The lock and score worked in every run; the findings are about what could break around them.

| OPS-2 | `src/gdn/daily.py:52-55`, `CLAUDE.md:37` | major | The one-shot 19:05 ET sleeper exits 2 on any dirty tracked file outside the daily paths, and a non-404 `gh` error escaped `daily.run` | `tools/eve_waiter.sh` retries `make daily-core` every 10 min from 19:05 to 23:30 ET until `_lock.json` is on origin; `daily.run` catches any lock-step exception and still commits and pushes | 1a02088, 47af692 | none automated (a shell loop; `bash -n` checked) |
| OPS-3 | `src/gdn/live.py:243`, spec §3.11 | major | The runner's curl reached the FAA, so its 08:17 EDT run on the eve will likely lock from a same-day snapshot | No code change: the preregistered rule allows it. `DECISIONS.md` records it as the expected path; the Mac runs nothing 08:00 to 08:45 ET that day and checks the release at 08:45 | 47af692 | none (a decision) |

## Round 2

Two fresh reviewers got this file and `git diff 062e00e..HEAD`: one for the code rows (`docs/build/review2_code.md`), one for the document rows (`docs/build/review2_docs.md`). Neither found a blocking or major finding, so under §7's stop rules ("A round with no blocking or major finding ends the review") the review ends here, with no round 3. What round 3's refuter would ask, whether a fix moved a §3 definition, broke determinism, a gate code or the preregistration's order, is checked by the final steps: `make all` changes no tracked file, `make check-determinism` prints identical, and the full gate's `faa`, `model` and `prereg` families rebuild the definitions and check the preregistration's commit order independently. Every closure held, except the three round 1 rows corrected above (C2/N1's wording, OPS-6's test, O4's reason). The code reviewer reverted each blocking and major fix in a copy and saw its test fail, reran `make all` in a fresh clone with no file changed, and repeated the conflict-during-a-lock case on real git. The document reviewer recomputed every figure round 1 added and found them right, and found the headline rule and §2's framing intact and the note at 7 pages.

Round 2's findings were all minor. I fixed those that were real defects rather than leave them open; each fix below was reverted in a copy and its test failed.
